catalog.label: Read telemetry and status
catalog.hint: Position, attitude, battery, flight mode, warnings, the vehicle list and the mission on board.

catalog.label: Read parameters
catalog.hint: The parameter list the vehicle reported, and a fresh download of it.

catalog.label: Change parameters
catalog.hint: Write one parameter at a time. Only names the connected firmware reported are accepted.

catalog.label: Missions
catalog.hint: Upload, start and clear a mission. Starting a mission arms the vehicle.

catalog.label: Arm and disarm
catalog.hint: Disarming in the air stops the motors.

catalog.label: Takeoff, land, return, hold and flight mode
Fly to a point
catalog.hint: Fly to one point or through several, at a height above home. From the ground or with several points this replaces the mission on board, arms the vehicle and takes off.

catalog.label: Direct control
catalog.hint: Stick inputs and velocity setpoints. Each lasts at most 5 s; without a new one the vehicle holds.

catalog.label: Other MAVLink commands
catalog.hint: One command from the list the capabilities name. Arming, takeoff, mode changes, calibration and flight termination are never on it.

catalog.label: Plugin tools
catalog.hint: Tools the installed plugins add, for the plugins switched on below. Each plugin has its own switches too.

result.instructions: Corvus GCS is a ground control station connected to a real vehicle (PX4 or ArduPilot). Every tool acts on that vehicle through the station, with the checks the operator's own buttons have. The operator decides which tools you have and may have to approve a call in Corvus first; a refused call says why. Read get_vehicle_state before acting, and check the result of every command. Heights are metres above home unless a tool says otherwise. Direct control lasts only for the duration you give; the vehicle holds when you stop sending.

plan.description: A Corvus mission plan. items is the route in order. Each item has a type: takeoff, waypoint, loiter_turns, loiter_time, land or rtl. Every type but rtl has lat, lon and alt (metres above home; land ignores alt). Optional fields: waypoint hold (s) and accept_radius (m); loiter_turns turns, radius (m) and direction (1 clockwise, -1 counterclockwise); loiter_time seconds, radius and direction; takeoff pitch (degrees). Plan level: name, speed (m/s).

result.name: manual_control
result.title: Stick input
result.description: Hold stick positions for duration_s seconds (MANUAL_CONTROL). x pitch forward, y roll right, r yaw right, each -1 to 1; z throttle 0 to 1, 0.5 holds height in position modes. Without a new call the vehicle holds.

vehicle.description: Vehicle id from list_vehicles. Leave out for the vehicle the operator flies.

result.name: set_velocity
result.title: Velocity
result.description: Fly at a velocity for duration_s seconds. vx, vy, vz in m/s: north, east, down, or with frame body forward, right, down. yaw_rate in degrees per second. Without a new call the vehicle holds. It sends setpoints only and never changes the flight mode: start it, then call set_flight_mode with the capabilities' velocity_mode while it runs (PX4 enters OFFBOARD only once setpoints arrive). Never on a plane.

result.title: Fly to
result.description: Fly to one point, or through several in order. alt is metres above home; a rover or boat ignores it. One point in the air leaves the mission on board alone. From the ground, or with several points, the points replace the mission on board and it is started, which arms the vehicle; an aircraft on the ground takes off.

result.name: manual_control
result.title: Stick input
result.description: Hold stick positions for duration_s seconds (MANUAL_CONTROL). x pitch forward, y roll right, r yaw right, each -1 to 1; z throttle 0 to 1, 0.5 holds height in position modes. Without a new call the vehicle holds.

vehicle.description: Vehicle id from list_vehicles. Leave out for the vehicle the operator flies.

result.name: set_velocity
result.title: Velocity
result.description: Fly at a velocity for duration_s seconds. vx, vy, vz in m/s: north, east, down, or with frame body forward, right, down. yaw_rate in degrees per second. Without a new call the vehicle holds. It sends setpoints only and never changes the flight mode: start it, then call set_flight_mode with the capabilities' velocity_mode while it runs (PX4 enters OFFBOARD only once setpoints arrive). Never on a plane.

result.title: Vehicles
result.description: Every vehicle Corvus hears, its links, and which one the operator flies. The ids are what the vehicle argument of other tools takes.

result.name: get_capabilities

result.description: What the connected autopilot can do through Corvus: the stack (PX4 or ArduPilot), hold and velocity modes, and the commands send_command accepts.

result.name: download_mission
result.title: Mission on board
result.description: Read the mission the vehicle holds, as a Corvus plan.

result.name: list_parameters
result.title: List parameters
result.description: The parameters the vehicle reported, name, value and type, at most 300 per call. Narrow it with a name prefix such as MPC_.

result.name: get_parameters
result.title: Read parameters
result.description: The current values of the named parameters.

result.name: download_parameters
result.title: Reload parameters
result.description: Ask the vehicle for its full parameter list again. Takes a few seconds; list_parameters answers once it is complete.

result.name: set_parameter
result.title: Change a parameter
result.description: Write one parameter. The name must be one the vehicle reported.

result.name: upload_mission
result.title: Upload a mission
result.description: Upload a mission plan to the vehicle. With start true it is started too, which arms the vehicle.

plan.description: A Corvus mission plan. items is the route in order. Each item has a type: takeoff, waypoint, loiter_turns, loiter_time, land or rtl. Every type but rtl has lat, lon and alt (metres above home; land ignores alt). Optional fields: waypoint hold (s) and accept_radius (m); loiter_turns turns, radius (m) and direction (1 clockwise, -1 counterclockwise); loiter_time seconds, radius and direction; takeoff pitch (degrees). Plan level: name, speed (m/s).

vehicle.description: Vehicle id from list_vehicles. Leave out for the vehicle the operator flies.

result.instructions: Corvus GCS is a ground control station connected to a real vehicle (PX4 or ArduPilot). Every tool acts on that vehicle through the station, with the checks the operator's own buttons have. The operator decides which tools you have and may have to approve a call in Corvus first; a refused call says why. Read get_vehicle_state before acting, and check the result of every command. Heights are metres above home unless a tool says otherwise. Direct control lasts only for the duration you give; the vehicle holds when you stop sending.
